projects.name: Camera System
projects.tagline: A customizable Roblox camera system with smooth follow, cinematic cutscenes, first person, shift lock, target lock and cross-platform controls.

blocks.value: A premium, fully customizable camera system built to make your game feel smoother, more polished, and way more immersive. Designed with flexibility in mind, it gives you everything you need to create a cinematic player experience without fighting clunky camera code.

It includes smooth follow and interpolation for fluid movement, dynamic FOV effects for speed and intensity, wind and shake effects for extra impact, and a custom first-person mode that feels clean and responsive. You also get custom shift lock, target lock-on, full cutscene support, and auto-adjustable zoom for a seamless experience across different gameplay styles.

Whether you are making a fast-paced action game, a story-driven experience, or a polished simulator, this system adapts to your needs. It is extremely customizable, easy to fit into different projects, and built with multi-platform support so it works naturally on PC, mobile, and console.
If you want a camera system that adds real quality, improves immersion, and gives your game a professional feel out of the box, this is the kind of upgrade players notice immediately.
Setting up the camera system only takes a few steps:

items: Import the provided .rbxm model into your place.
Move the CameraSystem folder into ReplicatedStorage.
Create a new LocalScript inside StarterPlayer > StarterPlayerScripts.
Paste the following code into the LocalScript:

blocks.value:
local CameraInitializer = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.CameraSystem.CameraInitializer)

CameraInitializer.init()
That's it! The camera system will automatically initialize when the player joins the game.

blocks.caption: Smoothly interpolates camera movement and rotation for responsive, natural-looking motion.
Create cinematic cutscenes with keyframes, camera filters, and seamless transitions.
A fully customizable shift lock with smooth transitions and configurable behavior.
An immersive first-person mode with customizable camera positioning and controls.
Lock onto targets with smooth tracking and effortless target switching.
Automatically adjusts camera zoom in tight spaces to prevent clipping and improve visibility.
Adds subtle camera movement to simulate wind and enhance environmental immersion.
Built for desktop, mobile, console, and gamepad with platform-specific controls.
Create dynamic camera shakes for impacts, explosions, and other gameplay events.

blocks.value: Usage guide for the CamConfig module.

items: Enabled — Master switch for the entire camera system. When false, all custom camera behavior is disabled.
DefaultCrosshair — The image asset used for the default crosshair in normal camera mode.
DefaultCrosshairSize — The size of the default crosshair in pixels.
DefaultCrossHairTransparency — The transparency of the default crosshair.
DefaultCamMaxDistance — The maximum distance the default camera can stay from the character.
CamFollowSpeed — Controls how quickly the camera follows the character movement.
MinZoom — The minimum allowed zoom distance.
MaxZoom — The maximum allowed zoom distance.
DefaultOffset — The default camera offset relative to the character.
DefaultCamMode — The default camera mode used when the system starts. Common values are free or locked.
DefaultCameraRotationMode — Defines how camera rotation behaves by default. Common values are default, disabled, or follow.
RotationSensibility — The sensitivity of camera rotation input.
ManualZoom — Enables or disables manual zoom input.
ZoomSensibility — Controls how fast zoom changes when the player zooms in or out.
ControlZoomIn — The controller key used to zoom in.
ControlZoomOut — The controller key used to zoom out.
PlayerMovementRotationEnabled — Enables character rotation based on movement.
PlayerMovementRotationLeftRight — Rotation influence applied when the player moves left or right.
PlayerMovementRotationFrontBack — Rotation influence applied when the player moves forward or backward.
RotatePlayerWhenPressingButtons — A list of keys that manually rotate the player.
FOVEffectContext — Determines where the FOV effect applies. Common values are first person, third person, none, or both.
CameraRollContext — Determines where camera roll effects apply.
CameraRollAmount — The maximum amount of roll applied to the camera.
WindEffectContext — Determines where wind effects apply.
WindEffectMinSpeed — The minimum speed required before wind effects start.
WindEffectIntensityFactor — A multiplier that controls how strong the wind effect is.
AdaptativeZoomOnClosedAmbient — Enables automatic zoom adjustment when the player is in a tight or closed space.
AdaptativeZoomOnClosedAmbientIntensity — Controls how strong the adaptive zoom effect becomes in closed spaces.
AdjustZoomBasedOnVehicle — Automatically adjusts zoom when the player is inside a vehicle.
DefaultFOV — The default field of view used by the camera.
FirstPersonDefaultFOV — The field of view used in first person mode.
SpeedFOVModifierFactor — How much player movement speed influences the FOV.
MaxCameraFOV — The maximum allowed field of view.
CustomShiftLock — Enables the custom shift lock system.
ShiftLockCamMaxDistance — The maximum camera distance while shift lock is active.
ShiftLockMobileButton — The mobile button used to toggle shift lock.
ShiftLockButtons — The keys or buttons used to toggle shift lock.
ShiftLockCrosshair — The image asset used for the shift lock crosshair.
ShiftLockCrossHairSize — The size of the shift lock crosshair in pixels.
ShiftLockCrossHairTransparency — The transparency of the shift lock crosshair.
ShiftLockOffset — The camera offset used while shift lock is active.
CustomFirstPerson — Enables the custom first person system.
FirstPersonButtons — The keys used to toggle first person mode.
FirstPersonMobileButton — The mobile button used to toggle first person mode.
FirstPersonMode — Defines how first person can be activated. Common values are disabled, key, zoom, or both.
FirstPersonCrosshair — The image asset used for the first person crosshair.
FirstPersonCrosshairSize — The size of the first person crosshair in pixels.
FirstPersonCrosshairTransparency — The transparency of the first person crosshair.
ShowBodyFirstPerson — Makes the character body visible while in first person.
CustomLockIn — Enables the target lock-in system.
LockInButtons — The inputs used to activate lock-in.
LockInMobileButton — The mobile button used to activate lock-in.
LockInCamMaxDistance — The maximum camera distance while locked onto a target.
LockInIconSize — The size of the lock-in icon.
AdjustZoomBasedOnTarget — Automatically adjusts zoom depending on the target’s size.
LockInIconTransparency — The transparency of the lock-in icon.
LockInIcon — The image asset used for the lock-in icon.
LockInSpin — Makes the lock-in icon spin while a target is locked.
LockInPump — Makes the lock-in icon pulse with a scaling animation.
LockInSpinSpeed — The speed of the lock-in spin animation.
LockInPumpSpeed — The speed of the lock-in pulsing animation.
LockInHighlight — Highlights the locked target.
LockInHighlightColor — The highlight color applied to the locked target.
LockInOffset — The camera offset used while locked onto a target.
DragToChangeTarget — Allows the player to drag to switch between targets while lock-in is active.

blocks.value: Every option is fully customizable, so you can tune the camera system for cinematic, competitive, realistic, or arcade-style gameplay.
The camera system is designed to be fully modular. You can use individual features independently or combine them to create more immersive gameplay.

Add dynamic camera shake for explosions, impacts, earthquakes, weapon recoil, or any other event. The shake system uses smooth interpolation instead of instantly changing the camera offset, producing natural-looking movement. Intensity controls the maximum displacement, Duration controls how long the shake lasts, and Frequency controls how quickly the shake changes direction.
Example:
CustomCameraState.shake(1.5, 0.4, 8)
Camera filters let you temporarily modify the game's visual appearance during gameplay or cutscenes. Each filter can control:

items: Brightness
Contrast
Saturation
Tint Color
Atmospheric Haze Color
Atmospheric Haze Density

blocks.value: Filters are tweened automatically, allowing smooth transitions between effects. You can also create your own filters using CameraFilter.new().
Example:

local filter = CameraFilter.new(
    0.2,
    0.4,
    -0.2,
    Color3.fromRGB(255,220,220),
    Color3.fromRGB(255,170,120),
    0.35
)

filter:apply(TweenInfo.new(1))

-- Remove the filter later
filter:remove(TweenInfo.new(1))
Camera keyframes define the path, rotation, FOV, and timing of a cutscene. Each keyframe stores three values:

items: cframe: The camera position and orientation.
fov: The field of view at that moment.
time: The timestamp used to place the keyframe in the cutscene timeline.

blocks.value: Creating Keyframes
You can create keyframes in four different ways depending on how much control you need:
1. CameraKeyframe.new(cframe, fov, time)
Use this when you already have a full CFrame prepared. This is the most direct constructor and gives you full control over both position and rotation.
Example:

local keyframe = CameraKeyframe.new(
    CFrame.new(0, 10, 20) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(180), 0),
    70,
    1.5
)
2. CameraKeyframe.fromPos(pos, fov, time)
Use this when you only want to place the camera at a position and do not need custom rotation. This creates a CFrame from the position only.
Example:
local keyframe = CameraKeyframe.fromPos(Vector3.new(0, 10, 20), 70, 1.5)
3. CameraKeyframe.fromPosAndRotation(pos, rotation, fov, time)
Use this when you want to define the camera position and a custom orientation manually. The rotation value is a Vector3 of Euler angles, using X, Y, and Z rotation values.
Example:

local keyframe = CameraKeyframe.fromPosAndRotation(
    Vector3.new(0, 10, 20),
    Vector3.new(0, math.rad(180), 0),
    70,
    1.5
)
4. CameraKeyframe.fromPosAndTargetPos(pos, targetpos, fov, time)
Use this when you want the camera to automatically face a specific point. The camera will look from pos toward targetpos, which is very useful for cinematic shots, dialogue scenes, and reveals.
Example:

local keyframe = CameraKeyframe.fromPosAndTargetPos(
    Vector3.new(0, 10, 20),
    Vector3.new(0, 5, 0),
    70,
    1.5
)

CameraCutscene is the main class responsible for playing cinematic camera sequences. It combines camera keyframes with optional features such as interpolation, target tracking, relative positioning, collision handling, visual filters, and cinematic UI.
Constructor:

CameraCutscene.new(
    keyframes,
    playMode,
    cutsceneUI,
    canPlayerMove,
    cameraFilter,
    target,
    reference,
    referenceRaycast,
    targetRaycast
)
keyframes
A table containing every CameraKeyframe that makes up the cutscene. The keyframes should be ordered by time, starting at 0 and increasing until the final shot.
playMode
Determines how the camera moves between keyframes.

items: None - Instantly switches between keyframes with no interpolation.
Linear - Smoothly interpolates between each keyframe using linear interpolation.
Catmull - Uses Catmull-Rom spline interpolation to generate smooth cinematic camera paths. This is the recommended mode for most cutscenes.

blocks.value: cutsceneUI

Enables the built-in cinematic UI. When enabled, cinematic bars and the cutscene interface automatically appear when the cutscene starts and disappear when it ends. Disable this if you want to create your own UI or use the camera system without any cinematic overlay.
canPlayerMove

Controls whether the player can move during the cutscene. If false, the player's WalkSpeed is temporarily set to 0 while the cutscene plays and restored afterward. This is ideal for story moments, intros, or scripted events. If true, the player can continue moving normally while the camera is controlled by the cutscene.
cameraFilter

An optional CameraFilter applied automatically when the cutscene begins. Filters can modify brightness, contrast, saturation, tint color, atmospheric haze, and more. Pass nil if you don't want any visual filter.
target

An optional Model or BasePart that the camera should continuously look at. Instead of using the rotation stored inside each keyframe, the camera automatically rotates every frame to keep this object centered. This is perfect for dialogue scenes, boss introductions, NPC interactions, or showcasing moving objects.
reference

An optional Model or BasePart used as the origin of the cutscene. Every keyframe becomes relative to this object instead of world space. This allows the exact same cutscene to be reused anywhere simply by changing the reference object. For example, you can create a vehicle intro once and reuse it for every vehicle by passing a different vehicle model as the reference.
referenceRaycast

Enables collision detection between the reference object and the camera. If a wall blocks the camera, it automatically moves closer instead of clipping through the geometry. Only affects cutscenes using a reference object.
targetRaycast

Enables collision detection between the target object and the camera. The system raycasts from the target toward the desired camera position and automatically adjusts the camera if an obstacle is found. This is especially useful when the target is moving through buildings, caves, or other enclosed environments.
Example

local cutscene = CameraCutscene.new(
    keyframes,
    "Catmull",
    true,
    false,
    CameraFilter.BlackAndWhite,
    boss,
    arena,
    true,
    true
)
CustomCameraState.setCutsceneAndPlay(cutscene, TweenInfo.new(1))
You can also provide TweenInfo when starting or stopping a cutscene to smoothly transition between gameplay and the cinematic camera.
Useful CameraState functions:

items: setCutsceneAndPlay(cutscene, transition) — Starts a cutscene immediately.
setCutsceneAndPlayAndStop(cutscene, startTransition, endTransition) — Automatically plays and removes the cutscene when it finishes.
stopCutscene(transition) — Stops the current cutscene while preserving it.
removeCutscene(transition) — Stops and completely removes the active cutscene.
resetCutscene() — Resets the cutscene back to its first keyframe.
isCutsceneActive() — Returns whether a cutscene is currently assigned.

projects.name: Movement System
projects.tagline: A modular, server-validated Roblox R6 movement framework with responsive traversal, stamina, procedural character animation, surface-aware effects, and configurable controls.

blocks.value: Movement System is a modular character-movement framework for Roblox Studio. It brings together directional locomotion, sprinting, stamina, directional dashes and ground rolls, sliding, vaulting, ledge climbing, wall running, swimming, narrow-surface balance, procedural R6 posing, and material-aware effects.

It is built around one central configuration module and a two-script bootstrap. Movement requests are validated by the server while client controllers handle responsive inputs, presentation, and appropriate motion effects. Most features can be tuned or disabled independently.

blocks.title: Current scope
blocks.value: The default experience targets R6. Full R15 behavior, comprehensive mobile controls for every traversal action, and certain roadmap features are not yet complete. Read the platform support section before using it in a production game.
Documentation reflects the current Movement-System repository configuration as of November 1, 2026. Values below are defaults, not fixed limits.
Import the full MovementSystem package into ReplicatedStorage. Its Client and Server subfolders, shared modules, configuration, animations and networking modules must remain together.

items: Place MovementSystem directly under ReplicatedStorage.
Create one regular Script in ServerScriptService.
Create one LocalScript in StarterPlayer > StarterPlayerScripts.
Paste the corresponding bootstrap code below and press Play.

blocks.value: Server bootstrap

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local system = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("MovementSystem")

require(system:WaitForChild("MovementSystemInitializer")).initServer()
Client bootstrap

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local system = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("MovementSystem")

require(system:WaitForChild("MovementSystemInitializer")).initClient()

blocks.title: Important
blocks.value: Use one server bootstrap and one client bootstrap. Remove previous Movement System installations before importing a new package, or duplicate controllers/remotes may conflict. The initializer handles subsequent character respawns.
For source-based development, the repository includes a default.project.json Rojo mapping and automated deployment tooling. Manual installation does not require Rojo.

Default controls are defined by feature-specific tables in Config.luau. All keys can be customized in the source configuration. Mobile buttons currently cover common actions, but not every traversal mechanic.
Keyboard and mouse

items: Move — W/A/S/D using normal Roblox movement.
Jump / climb a held ledge — Space.
Sprint — Left Ctrl (toggle by default).
Crouch — hold C; pressing C while sprinting forward triggers slide.
Dash / ground roll — Q, with movement direction determining the action direction.
Vault — Space near a valid obstacle, or automatically while sprinting forward.
Ledge grab — hold right mouse button close to a reachable edge; A/D to shimmy.
Drop from ledge — release right mouse button or press Left Ctrl.
Wall jump — Space while wall running.
Swim up / down — Space / Left Alt while swimming.

blocks.value: Gamepad and touch

items: Gamepad sprint — press L3.
Gamepad dash — B; crouch/slide — RB / R1.
Gamepad ledge grab — hold LT / L2; swim down — B; jump/swim up — A.
Mobile — touch controls are available for sprint, crouch/slide, dash and swimming descent.

blocks.title: Platform support
blocks.value: Some inputs vary by action state. Ledge grab currently has no dedicated mobile grab button, and full mobile/gamepad traversal coverage is still being developed. Test bindings together with any external combat or camera system.
The framework supports directional walk/run animation selection, smoothed acceleration and stopping, directional intent, idle rotation, turning animations, and action-state restrictions.

items: Config.Movement.WalkSpeed — default 12 studs/s.
Config.Sprint.Speed — default 26 studs/s.
Config.Movement.Acceleration — per-state acceleration and idle deceleration.
Config.Movement.Direction — direction-specific movement multipliers and diagonal normalization.
Config.Movement.Rotation — character rotation and response speed.
Config.DirectionalAnimations — directional clip detection and blending.

blocks.value: The animation system also contains separate clips for forward, backward, left, and right movement. Turn-step animations react to actual character yaw rather than requiring camera rotation data.

Sprinting is a server-validated state with optional stamina consumption. It cannot begin while crouching, balancing, seated, or during certain action locks. The default activation mode is Toggle; Hold is supported, while RepeatedTap is not yet independently implemented.

Config.Sprint.Speed = 26
Config.Sprint.Mode = "Toggle" -- or "Hold"
Config.Sprint.Input.Desktop.Key = Enum.KeyCode.LeftControl
Config.Sprint.Input.Gamepad.Key = Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL3

Directional inertia is handled separately by Client/InertiaController and InertiaConfig.luau. Ground dash/roll direction changes have additional steering and exit-redirection tuning under Config.Dash.Motion.
Stamina is shared between sprinting and traversal. The server controls authoritative values and replicates stamina to attributes for UI and effects.

items: Config.Stamina.Max / StartValue — 200.
Config.Stamina.Sprint.DrainPerSecond — 10.
Config.Stamina.Jump.Cost — 15.
Config.Stamina.Regeneration.PerSecond — 14, after a 1-second delay.
Config.Stamina.Swimming.DrainPerSecond — 8 when actively swimming.
Config.Stamina.UI.Style — Wheel (default) or Bar.

blocks.value: Change stamina and HUD settings

Config.Stamina.Max = 200
Config.Stamina.StartValue = 200
Config.Stamina.Regeneration.PerSecond = 14
Config.Stamina.UI.Enabled = true
Config.Stamina.UI.Style = "Wheel"
Config.Stamina.UI.Wheel.Diameter = 70
Config.Stamina.UI.Wheel.HideWhenFull = true

The wheel appears near the character when stamina is used and hides after recovery; its offset, size, colors and fade behavior are configurable. An infinite-stamina testing option exists, but the server restricts it using AllowedUserIds or explicit permissions. It is not enabled for all public players by default.
The Dash feature provides an airborne directional dash and a physically distinct ground roll. You do not need to enable the separate, currently unused Config.Roll roadmap module for ground rolling.

items: Input — Q on keyboard, B on gamepad, DASH touch button.
Air dash — default peak speed 35 studs/s; duration 0.58 s.
Ground roll — default peak speed 28 studs/s (35 × 0.80), physical duration 1.08 s.
Air limit — one dash per airtime by default; refreshed on landing.
Stamina — 15 per dash.
Animation — full ground-roll clip with configurable crossfades into locomotion.
Motion — steer during the ground roll and blend away outdated sideways momentum when exiting.
Effects — ground roll uses surface dust; airborne dash can emit Lines and AirRift effects.

blocks.value:
Config.Dash.Speed = 35
Config.Dash.GroundSpeedMultiplier = 0.80
Config.Dash.GroundDuration = 1.08
Config.Dash.Air.MaxDashes = 1
Config.Dash.Stamina.Cost = 15
Config.Dash.Motion.GroundSteeringResponse = 10
Config.Dash.Motion.GroundExitRedirect = 0.8

blocks.title: Tuning
blocks.value: The physical action duration and visual animation timing are separate. Adjust Config.Dash.Motion for steering/braking, and Config.Dash.Animation for fade and playback. Avoid shortening the animation unintentionally when tuning physical movement.

Hold C to crouch. While running forward on the ground, press C to start a server-approved slide instead. Releasing the key during the slide allows sprint to resume; holding it through the end transitions into crouch.

items: Crouch speed — 8 studs/s.
Slide start speed — 28 studs/s.
Minimum start speed — 18 studs/s.
Slide duration — 1.0 s, with configurable friction and slope response.
Slide stamina cost — 5; cooldown 0.5 s.
R6 crouch pose — optional RootJoint visual offset; no manual root-physics lowering.

blocks.value:
Config.Crouch.Speed = 8
Config.Crouch.Input.Key = Enum.KeyCode.C
Config.Crouch.RootOffset.LowerStuds = 1.0

Config.Slide.Movement.InitialSpeed = 28
Config.Slide.Movement.Duration = 1.0
Config.Slide.Movement.Friction = 8
Config.Slide.Stamina.Cost = 5

blocks.title: Not yet implemented
blocks.value: Automatic crouching beneath a low ceiling is a planned feature; Config.Crouch.Adaptive.Enabled is false by default.

Vaulting allows players to cross suitable waist-height obstacles without conventional jumping. The client detects likely candidates, the server validates the wall geometry and landing clearance, and the client follows the approved trajectory.

items: Activation — automatically during forward sprint, or with Space while moving toward an obstacle.
Obstacle height — default 2–4.5 studs.
Obstacle depth — default 0.2–3.5 studs.
Detection — supports wall tops made of joined Parts, including separate caps.
Trajectory — eased climb, aligned rotation toward the wall, controlled forward crossing and gravity-driven release.
Cooldown — 0.45 s; animations vary with obstacle geometry.

blocks.value:
Config.Vault.Enabled = true
Config.Vault.Activation.Automatic = true
Config.Vault.Detection.MinimumHeight = 2
Config.Vault.Detection.MaximumHeight = 4.5
Config.Vault.Detection.MaximumDepth = 3.5
Config.Vault.Motion.TraversalSpeedMultiplier = 1.5

A high or unreachable wall should remain a normal jump/ledge-grab candidate instead of being forcibly converted into a vault. If a vault is not triggered, check obstacle dimensions, forward input, collision geometry, and the client/server action state.

Hold right mouse button (or LT/L2 on a gamepad) close to a reachable ledge to hang. While hanging, press A/D to traverse sideways, press Space to climb, or release the grab input / press Left Ctrl to drop.

items: Reach — default detection radius 9 studs; maximum ledge height above the root 9.5 studs.
Hanging position — root about 2 studs below the ledge top, with a 1-stud wall offset.
Shimmy speed — 4 studs/s; geometry is checked while moving.
Hand clearance — movement is blocked when nearby upper geometry obstructs the direction of the reaching arm.
Stamina — drains 10 per second while hanging by default; exhaustion automatically releases the ledge.
Climb — server-validated climb path and destination with blended R6 arm posing.

blocks.value:
Config.LedgeGrab.Detection.Distance = 9
Config.LedgeGrab.Detection.MaximumGrabHeight = 9.5
Config.LedgeGrab.Movement.RootBelowTop = 2.0
Config.LedgeGrab.Movement.ShimmySpeed = 4

Config.LedgeGrab.Hold.DrainStamina = true
Config.LedgeGrab.Hold.StaminaDrainPerSecond = 10

blocks.title: Control note
blocks.value: Ledge grab can start from the ground when a ledge is within reach, because RequireAirborne is false by default. A dedicated touch-grab control is still part of the mobile-controls roadmap.

Wall running engages automatically near a valid side wall while airborne and moving. The character follows the wall with a stable wall-relative orientation; pressing Space triggers a wall jump away from the surface.

items: Minimum approach speed — 4 studs/s.
Wall detection — approximately 3 studs from the character.
Travel speed — 24 studs/s with controlled descent at 7 studs/s.
Stamina — requires at least 5 to enter and drains 12/s.
Wall jump — configurable outward, forward and upward impulses.
Cooldown — 0.15 s; camera tilt and VFX can be configured.

blocks.value:
Config.WallRun.Activation.Automatic = true
Config.WallRun.Activation.MinimumSpeed = 4
Config.WallRun.Movement.Speed = 24
Config.WallRun.Movement.DescentSpeed = 7
Config.WallRun.Jump.UpwardSpeed = 70
Config.WallRun.Stamina.DrainPerSecond = 12

Wall-run movement uses constrained vertical speed, rather than simply scaling Roblox gravity. The retained Config.WallRun.Gravity table is a compatibility setting, not the current primary vertical-motion implementation.
Swimming uses Roblox's native Terrain Water and Humanoid swimming state. The package does not generate a demonstration lake, alter terrain, or replace native water physics.

items: Swim — native movement with configurable surface and underwater poses.
Ascend — Space / gamepad A; descend — Left Alt / gamepad B / DIVE touch button.
Stamina — 8 per second during active swimming; exhaustion limits swim control until recovery.
Surface splash — VFX follows physical R6 arm/water contact, alternating arms with cooldown rather than a fixed rhythm.
Entry impact — a separate water-entry splash for real downward contact.
Sound — default continuous swimming loop is muted; arm stroke splashes are visual-only.

blocks.value:
Config.Swimming.Enabled = true
Config.Swimming.Input.DescendKey = Enum.KeyCode.LeftAlt
Config.Swimming.Effects.ArmContact.StrokeCooldown = 0.18
Config.Swimming.Effects.MuteNativeSwimmingLoop = true
Config.Stamina.Swimming.DrainPerSecond = 8

blocks.title: Testing
blocks.value: Create Terrain Water in Roblox Studio and test with an R6 avatar. Regular Parts colored blue are not treated as swimmable water.

When the player walks onto sufficiently narrow geometry, balance detection samples real nearby support and can temporarily restrict sprint. Local balance posing gradually extends arms while movement continues.

items: Config.Balance — narrow-surface checks, drop detection, animation blend and sprint restrictions.
Config.BalanceMovement — reconstructs the local path centerline and tangent, including curved or slightly discontinuous paths.
Tracked movement — adjusts Humanoid:MoveTo() direction toward the sampled route, instead of anchoring the character.
Exit — clearly sideways movement returns control to normal movement.

blocks.value:
Config.Balance.Enabled = true
Config.Balance.BlockSprint = true
Config.BalanceMovement.Enabled = true
Config.BalanceMovement.CenteringGain = 2.75
Config.BalanceMovement.PathSampleInterval = 0.05

The package includes a centralized DefaultAnimations.luau catalog and server-side character animation handling. It preloads animation assets asynchronously and disables the character's default Roblox Animate LocalScript to prevent two locomotion animators competing.

items: Locomotion — idle, directional walking/running, turn-step, jump, falling and landing.
Traversal — crouch, slide, dash/roll, wall run, vault, ledge hang and climb.
Swimming — surface and underwater sequences with separate posing and blending.
Playback — adjustable fades, track speed and state-driven transitions.

blocks.value: Replacing an animation
Edit the corresponding entry in MovementSystem/DefaultAnimations.luau before running the game. The following shows the same constructor used by that module:

-- Example: replace the directional forward-run clip.
RunForward = ActionAnimation.new(
    "rbxassetid://YOUR_ANIMATION_ID",
    0.75, -- playback multiplier
    0.35, -- fade time
    true, -- looped
    {}
),

blocks.title: Compatibility
blocks.value: Animation assets must be available to the experience and authored for the intended rig. R6 is the currently configured target. A config flag alone does not provide full R15 equivalents.

Footstep playback is tied to detected foot contacts, not a fixed looping timer. The client samples animated R6 legs (or R15 feet where supported), determines the actual surface under the contacting foot, and plays a spatial, single-impact sound.

items: Material mapping — grass, concrete, wood, metal, fabric, wet surfaces and sand profiles.
Overrides — surface FootstepProfile Attributes or FootstepProfile_* CollectionService tags.
Turn steps — contact-driven sounds with an angular fallback for certain turn animations.
Audio behavior — one-shot trimming, contact cooldowns, volume multipliers and spatial distance limits.
Landing — a separate real-airborne-cycle landing impact, with a louder high-drop option.
Configuration — FootstepConfig.luau and Config.Footsteps.

blocks.value: Override a surface's sound

blocks.file: Any server Script, after the Part exists
blocks.value:
-- Mark a metal walkway to use the Metal sound profile.
local walkway = workspace:WaitForChild("MetalWalkway")
walkway:SetAttribute("FootstepProfile", "Metal")
The controller resolves explicit overrides first, then physical material and the default profile. The default Roblox running, jumping and landing sounds can be muted to avoid duplicate impacts.

blocks.title: Asset note
blocks.value: Configured Creator Store samples are trimmed to short impact windows by the runtime. Always verify sound permissions and timing in your own experience.
Material-aware dust and footprints react to accepted physical foot contacts. Grounded movement produces brief contact bursts; dash and landing events have their own one-shot effect profiles.

items: Dust materials — Ground, Sand, Snow and Mud by default; no procedural dust on concrete or metal.
Step dust — burst intensity scales with speed, while event timing comes from actual foot plants.
Dash dust — separate burst size and particle count.
Landing dust — larger burst for genuine ground contact after an airborne cycle.
Footprints — flat surface marks with a default 5-second lifetime and 1.6-second fade.
Files — DustConfig.luau and FootprintConfig.luau.

blocks.value:
-- DustConfig.luau
DustConfig.Step.SizeMultiplier = 2.325
DustConfig.Landing.SizeMultiplier = 3.0

-- FootprintConfig.luau (separate file)
FootprintConfig.Lifetime = 5
FootprintConfig.FadeTime = 1.6

High falls can also have their own fall/landing animation and impact audio. The separate HardLanding roadmap feature toggle is disabled by default; it should not be confused with normal landing dust and sound.
Dedicated action SFX live under Config.ActionSounds. Footstep and landing sounds are configured independently in FootstepConfig.luau. Sounds must be permitted for the Roblox experience.

items: ActionSounds.Jump — standard jump and wall-jump sound.
ActionSounds.AirForwardDash — airborne forward dash effect.
ActionSounds.Dash — other dash/roll actions; reused where applicable.
FootstepConfig.Events.Step.VolumeMultiplier — step loudness.
FootstepConfig.Events.Land.VolumeMultiplier — landing loudness and high-drop multiplier.

Procedural animation adds small, reactive offsets over authored clips rather than replacing the primary animation controller.

items: R6 Leg IK — independently samples both legs and adjusts contact on uneven ground; includes planted and moving-foot logic.
Body avoidance — checks nearby obstacles and applies restrained head/torso reactions without unnecessary large lean.
Balance pose — adjusts shoulders and head as narrow-surface movement increases.
Ledge pose — aligns arms with the ledge and animates alternating shimmy reaches.
Swimming pose — surface and underwater alignment with smooth orientation changes.
Performance — distance and update-rate controls for remote-character procedural presentation.

The public settings are defined in ReplicatedStorage/MovementSystem/Config.luau. Supporting profiles are separated into dedicated modules for inertia, footsteps, dust and footprints. Change source values before runtime: the returned configuration tables are recursively frozen.

Both a global Config.Features.FeatureName flag and a feature table's Enabled flag may be checked. These values are evaluated at controller initialization; restarting the character or package may be required for changes to take effect.
Main configuration groups

items: Movement, Sprint, Stamina — speeds, control, stamina and UI.
Dash, Slide, Vault, LedgeGrab, WallRun — traversal tuning.
Swimming, Balance, BalanceMovement — environment-specific movement.
Animations, DirectionalAnimations, R6LegIK, R6BodyAvoidance — motion and procedural presentation.
Footsteps, ActionSounds, Performance, Debug — effects, optimization and diagnostics.

blocks.title: Compatibility
blocks.value: Older aliases such as Config.WalkSpeed and Config.SprintSpeed exist, but new integrations should use the grouped settings.

Each supported feature can have Attribute requirements, blocked Attributes, a CanStart resolver and a CanContinue resolver. Author the integration in Config.luau; do not try to mutate the frozen required table at runtime.
Unlock wall running with a player Attribute
Set the corresponding Attribute on the player through a trusted server script when the ability is unlocked.

-- Example only: run after your own trusted unlock validation.
player:SetAttribute("HasWallRun", true)
Block sprinting while stunned

Config.Sprint.Access.CanStart = function(context)
    if context.Character:GetAttribute("Stunned") == true then
        return false, "Stunned"
    end
    return true
end
Dynamic sprint speed

Config.Sprint.Speed = function(context)
    local level = context.Player
        and context.Player:GetAttribute("SprintLevel")
        or 0

    return 26 + level * 2
end

Context includes Player, Character, Humanoid, RootPart, Speed, IsServer, Feature and other movement data. Authoritative features enforce permission checks on the server; client-only checks are not a security boundary.
Feature lifecycle callbacks are declared in Config.*.Callbacks; global action hooks are in Config.Callbacks. They are useful for UI, statistics, combat rules and custom effects.

Config.Sprint.Callbacks.OnStart = function(context)
    print("Sprint started:", context.Player)
end

Config.Sprint.Callbacks.OnBlocked = function(context, reason)
    warn("Sprint blocked:", reason)
end

Config.Callbacks.OnActionStarted = function(feature, context)
    print("Movement action:", feature, context.Character)
end

Available feature lifecycle hooks include OnAttempt, OnStart, OnUpdate, OnStop, OnBlocked and cooldown notifications where the controller emits them. There are also integration tables for camera, combat, status, skills and UI.

blocks.title: Integration guidance
blocks.value: The system can initialize a compatible ReplicatedStorage.CameraSystem.CameraInitializer automatically. When integrating your own combat system, coordinate action ownership and controls instead of adding a second movement controller for the same action.

Movement requests are checked on the server, and relevant state is replicated with Attributes. This allows a HUD, ability system or NPC logic to read movement state without depending on every internal controller.

items: MovementSprinting — whether sprint is active.
MovementCrouching — crouch state.
MovementBalancing — balance state.
MovementAction — current traversal/action state.
MovementStamina / MovementMaxStamina — replicated stamina values.
MovementAirDashesUsed — number of air dashes spent in the current airborne period.
MovementSwimExhausted — swimming exhaustion state.
MovementInfiniteStamina / MovementInfiniteStaminaAllowed — permission-gated testing state.

blocks.value: Attributes may belong to the Player or Character, depending on the feature. Refer to Config.Character.Attributes, Config.Networking.StateAttributes and the individual controller before consuming one in a different system.

local player = game:GetService("Players").LocalPlayer

local function onSprintChanged()
    local isSprinting = player:GetAttribute("MovementSprinting") == true
    print("Sprinting:", isSprinting)
end

player:GetAttributeChangedSignal("MovementSprinting"):Connect(onSprintChanged)
onSprintChanged()

blocks.title: Security
blocks.value: Keep critical gameplay authorization and private information in server-only code. The reusable movement package is stored in ReplicatedStorage, which clients can read.

Server-side modules validate shared movement states, while local controllers handle inputs, interpolation, animation layers and visually responsive effects. Only the two small bootstrap scripts live outside the MovementSystem folder.

items: MovementSystemInitializer — one-time server/client entry points and character setup.
Server/MovementService — core sprint, stamina, crouch and state management.
Server/DashService, SlideService, VaultService, WallRunService, LedgeService — action validation.
Server/CharacterAnimationService and Server/Animation — shared animation handling.
Client/*Controller — input, local traversal, procedural poses, surface contacts and VFX.
Network.luau and ConfigRuntime.luau — remotes, config resolution, permission checks and callback dispatch.

blocks.value: Optimization settings include distance-limited remote procedural animation, sampled foot contact, update intervals, pooled surface audio and configurable effect lifetimes. Adjust Config.Performance and the dedicated effect configs after profiling your own place.
Nothing happens when I press an action key

Check that both bootstrap scripts are running, the package is under ReplicatedStorage, the corresponding feature is enabled, and another action has not locked movement. Check Output for [MovementSystem] warnings.
Animations do not play or characters appear frozen

Confirm the avatar uses R6, verify animation asset permissions, and remove duplicate copies of the system or competing animation controllers. The initializer disables the default Animate script on purpose.
Vault or ledge grab does not detect a wall

Verify the geometry is collidable and reachable, check wall dimensions and clearance, and make sure sprint/vault and ledge control modes are not competing. Test with simple anchored Parts before complex meshes.
I hear two footsteps or the wrong surface
Check for another footstep script, confirm default Roblox contact sounds are muted, then review FootstepConfig.Contact, Events.Step.MaxPlayTime and any FootstepProfile override.
There is no ground dust or swimming splash

Dust is only emitted for configured loose materials such as Ground, Sand, Snow and Mud. Swimming effects require real Roblox Terrain Water and qualifying physical contact; blue Parts and fully submerged arm strokes are not equivalent.
My mobile action does not appear
Verify that the feature's mobile input is enabled and has CreateTouchButton = true when supported. Some traversal features still lack dedicated touch input.
The current public documentation describes the modules that exist in the current source, not every unfinished item in older roadmap checklists.

items: R6 — primary supported rig and target for procedural arm/leg systems.
R15 — the complete rig-specific animation/procedural implementation is not yet enabled by default.
Mobile — sprint, crouch/slide, dash and swim-down controls exist; complete traversal button support is still in progress.
Roadmap feature tables — the separate Roll, Dive, HardLanding and HardBrake modules are disabled, even though ground rolling is already provided by Dash.
Automatic low-clearance crouch — not yet implemented.
Custom animation assets — must match the intended rig and be accessible to the experience.
